THIS WRIT PETITION IS FILED UNDER ARTICLE 226 OF THE CONSTITUTION OF
INDIA PRAYING FOR A DIRECTION TO THE RESPONDENTS TO PROCESS THE
PETITIONER'S APPLICATION FOR MUTATION DATED 12.04.2024 AND TO ISSUE
THE REVISED RECORD OF RIGHTS.

ORDER WAS PRONOUNCED AS UNDER:

1. The petitioner is the recorded owner of agricultural land bearing Sy. No. 145/2 of Begur Village, Bengaluru South Taluk, having acquired the same by registered sale deed dated 08.03.2024. The petitioner applied for mutation on 12.04.2024. Despite the lapse of nearly two years, the application remains pending without disposal.

2. It is the contention of the petitioner that repeated representations to the second respondent and the third respondent have not yielded any response. The petitioner contends that the inaction violates the timelines prescribed under the Karnataka Land Revenue Rules, 1966.

3. Per contra, the learned Additional Government Advocate submits that the application is under verification and a decision will be taken in due course.

4. Having heard the learned counsel for the petitioner and the learned Additional Government Advocate, and on a perusal of the records, this Court is of the view that the second respondent has failed to discharge the statutory duty cast upon it. The Karnataka Land Revenue Rules require disposal of mutation applications within a reasonable period, which has been judicially construed as not exceeding ninety days from receipt.

5. In view of the foregoing, the present petition is disposed of with the following directions.

6. The third respondent is directed to complete field verification of the petitioner's application within four weeks from the date of this order. The second respondent is directed to pass a final order on the mutation application within sixty days from the date of this order. The first respondent is directed to ensure compliance and file a compliance affidavit within ninety days from the date of this order.

SD/-

(SURESH KUMAR)
